hypotheses.justification: Local compactness is used only to get a compact neighbourhood U of x₀, so that ‖f‖ is bounded on U ×ˢ s. That bound holds without it. Since s is compact, {x₀} ×ˢ s is compact. ‖f.uncurry‖ is continuous, so it is bounded there by some M (e.g. via `IsCompact.bddAbove_image`). The set {p | ‖f.uncurry p‖ < M+1} is open and contains {x₀} ×ˢ s. `generalized_tube_lemma` (Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean) gives an open u ∋ x₀ and an open v ⊇ s with u ×ˢ v ⊆ that set. Take u in place of U. Then ‖f x y‖ ≤ M+1 for x ∈ u and y ∈ s, and u ∈ 𝓝 x₀. The rest of the proof is unchanged: `continuousAt_of_dominated` only needs [FirstCountableTopology X], and the constant bound is integrable on s because s is compact and μ is locally finite. The statement is therefore still true and provable with this one hypothesis deleted. Nothing else in the statement mentions LocallyCompactSpace X. The degenerate cases (X empty, s empty, E trivial) are all fine.
